diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, we will lump all zero order terms

issues.failure_explanation: Only the convective term is given a quadrature rule. The term ve(U_y,V_y) is integrated exactly, and for V=psi_i(x)psi^j(y) it equals -ve * sum_n (int phi_n psi_i dx) * kbar_j * delta_y^2 U_{n,j}. The integrals int phi_n psi_i dx are nonzero for n=i-1,i,i+1, so this couples x-neighbours with weights that are not Q^C_{i,j}. The scheme (finite-difference), which carries the whole analysis, has only -ve Q^C_{i,j} delta_y^2 U_{i,j}. That scheme follows only if an extra lumping of this term is imposed, and the paper does not state one. Without it, the claimed equivalence, and with it the discrete minimum principle (Lemma 2), is not shown for the method defined by the weak form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the additional quadrature or lumping rule for the ve(U_y,V_y) term that yields Q^C_{i,j} delta_y^2 U_{i,j}, and verify that it reproduces (finite-difference).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is stated for the solution of (discrete-weak-form), but every lemma analyses L^N from (finite-difference). The link between the two is unsupported as written, and inverse monotonicity of the actual weak-form method is not established.
issues.title: Stated Petrov-Galerkin scheme does not produce the analysed finite-difference operator (y-diffusion term not lumped)
issues.why_classification: A short local clarification of the quadrature restores the stated scheme and keeps all analysis unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's first bound gives the coefficient alpha/(1-e^{-rhobar_i}) on D^-Z. Since h_i >= h_{i+1}, rhobar_i >= rhobar_{i+1}, so alpha/(1-e^{-rhobar_i}) <= alpha/(1-e^{-rhobar_{i+1}}). The second inequality therefore goes the wrong way whenever h_i > h_{i+1}, i.e. at the transition point. Counterexample: take D^-Z_i=1 and D^+Z_i=0 at x_i=1-tau_x. Then L^N Z is at most 2 max(a)/(1-e^{-1}), while the claimed bound is at least ve/h, which is of order N/ln N. Applied to Z=e^{-alpha(1-x)/ve}, the bracket in the corollary is (1-e^{-rhobar_i})/h_i - (1-e^{-rhobar_{i+1}})/h_{i+1}. This is nonpositive for h_i>h_{i+1}, not the stated positive bound, and it has the wrong dimension.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop Cor1 and prove the barrier inequalities L^N e^{-alpha(1-x)/ve} >= 0 and L^N e^{2x/alpha} >= e^{2x/alpha} directly from the monotonicity of sigma, handling the transition node separately.
issues.overall_effect: The barrier inequalities for e^{-alpha(1-x)/ve} (Lemma 4) and e^{2x/alpha} (Lemma 5) are justified via Cor1 and are unsupported at transition nodes. The nodal bounds for the layer components and the global theorem rest on them.
issues.title: Corollary 1 is false when h_i differs from h_{i+1}; Lemma 4 barrier inequality does not follow
issues.why_classification: The barrier properties are very likely true and provable by a contained direct computation. The corollary as stated and its use must be replaced, which is more than a one-line fix.

issues.failure_explanation: tau_x = 0.5 occurs exactly when 0.5 <= 2 ve ln N/alpha, i.e. alpha/(2 ve) <= 2 ln N. Then e^{-alpha tau_x/ve} = e^{-alpha/(2 ve)} >= N^{-2}, so the inequality is reversed (for ve of order 1 it is a constant). Hence |w_E| <= C N^{-2} for x_i <= 1-tau_x is also false in the uniform case. In that case one has instead ve^{-1} <= C ln N, and the error bound must come from a different argument, which the proof only gestures at ('sigma(rho) <= C').
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat tau_x=0.5 separately using ve^{-1} <= C ln N in the truncation estimates, and use the barrier e^{-alpha(1-x)/(2 ve)} with L^N barrier >= C/ve to obtain the (N^{-1} ln N)^2 bound.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform-mesh branch of the W_E error bound (and, through Lemma 4, the global bound for ve >= alpha/(4 ln N)) is not correctly justified as written.
issues.title: Reversed inequality for uniform horizontal mesh in Lemma 4
issues.why_classification: The error terms are already of the form N^{-2} times powers of ve^{-1} <= C ln N, so a short local case argument recovers the same bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The (M^{-1} ln M)^2 term for W_N and W_S comes from ve*k_j^2*|d^4 w_N/dy^4| on the fine vertical mesh (k_j ~ sqrt(ve) ln M/M), which needs |d^4 w_N/dy^4| <= C ve^{-2}. Section 2 and Lemma 1 give y-derivatives of w_N, w_S only for j=2,3, and only x-derivatives (i=3,4) in the extension. The bounds on the mixed derivatives d^3u/(dy^2 dx) and d^3u/(dx^2 dy) used in the truncation estimates for w_N and w_S are also missing. With only the third derivative the y-truncation error is O(ln M/M), i.e. first order.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the fourth y-derivative and mixed-derivative bounds for w_N and w_S, for example by extending the parabolic-layer expansion argument of the cited reference, and add them to Lemma 1.
issues.overall_effect: The second-order bound (M^{-1} ln M)^2 for W_N-w_N and W_S-w_S, and hence the global theorem, rely on unproven derivative estimates for the characteristic layers, the hardest part of the decomposition.
issues.title: Lemma 5 uses y-derivative bounds for w_N, w_S (and mixed derivatives) that are never established
issues.why_classification: A new but contained regularity lemma, following the same technique as the existing bounds, is needed. The overall architecture and rate stay the same.

issues.failure_explanation: w_N has no decay in x: its x-derivatives are bounded by ve^{3-i} e^{-(1-y)/sqrt(ve)}. By (trunc-error-sharp), the x-part of the truncation error on a uniform horizontal stretch is of order h_i^2 with no factor e^{-alpha(1-x)/ve}. In the coarse x-region h_i ~ 1/N, so the true error is ~N^{-2}, whereas the stated bound is ~N^{-4}/ve, which is smaller for ve > N^{-2}. The proposed barrier has an x-decaying term and a term (M^{-1} ln M)^2 x_i, so for independent N and M it cannot dominate an N^{-2} truncation error. A term of the form (N^{-1})^2 x_i is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the x-truncation error for w_N and w_S as C h_i^2 (no exponential factor) and add the barrier C N^{-2}(ln N)^2 x_i to the stated barrier.
issues.overall_effect: The barrier argument for W_N and W_S does not follow as written. The conclusion is plausible (M=N works) but is not proved for general N, M.
issues.title: Lemma 5 truncation error for w_N carries a regular-layer exponential factor in x and the barrier cannot absorb the true error
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of an estimate and a barrier term (B_1 is already available) and leaves the lemma's bound unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The bilinear interpolation bound is quoted from another paper without checking its hypotheses against the bounds of Section 2. Here |d^2 w_E/dy^2| is only bounded by C ve^{-1} e^{-alpha(1-x)/(4ve)}. On the coarse vertical mesh (k ~ 2/M) inside the x-layer, the standard estimate k^2 |w_yy| is of order ve^{-1} M^{-2}, not uniformly small in ve. No bound on d w_E/dy is given to cap it at order M^{-1}. The paper's own nodal bound for W_E - w_E is only M^{-1}(M^{-1} ln M)^{2/3}, which reflects exactly this weaker y-regularity, yet the interpolation error is asserted to be (M^{-1} ln M)^2. So the term u - u_I, and hence the final bound, is not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Verify or prove an interpolation estimate for w_E using only the derivative bounds actually available, and state the resulting global rate with that interpolation term included.
issues.overall_effect: The passage from nodal to global (L-infinity) error is not justified as stated, so the advertised global rate may be worse than claimed for the regular-layer component.
issues.title: Global bound uses a cited interpolation estimate that is inconsistent with the paper's own w_E derivative bounds
issues.why_classification: A contained re-estimate of the interpolation error is needed. The final rate may weaken somewhat but stays comparable.
